uncited: This family extends 3D Gaussian Splatting to model complex, view-dependent lighting effects such as specular highlights and anisotropic reflections, which standard isotropic spherical Gaussians cannot capture accurately.
All methods in this family share the goal of decomposing appearance into geometric and directional components to support view-dependent shading.
**Primitive Representation:** Gaussians are augmented with parameters beyond position, covariance, and opacity.
**Directional Evaluation:** The contribution of a Gaussian to a pixel is modulated by the viewing direction relative to the primitive's orientation.
Standard 3D Gaussian Splatting uses spherical harmonics to encode view-dependent color, which struggles with high-frequency specularities and anisotropic reflections.
Recent advances introduced anisotropic representations and PBR integration to address these limitations.
These methods are used in high-fidelity 3D reconstruction, digital twins, and virtual production where realistic lighting interactions are critical.
